kind: Experimental dialogue-shooting spike, replacing the interrupted button-target idea

implementation.after: Bithumb Original after happiness until replay; dialogue floats in a separate Three.js FX scene
implementation.target: Current interviewer line, split into <=18 code-point chunks; three visible slots with remaining chunks queued
implementation.interaction: Aim/click/tap; keys 1/2/3 outside text fields; accessible target buttons
implementation.hit: Same letter texture broken into 32 triangles in one batched mesh, fades and disposes after ~1.05s
implementation.reply: Text/voice conversation unchanged; shooting does not submit an answer, advance anger counters or call AI
implementation.pause: Room/editor pause preserves current targets; reduced-motion uses static targets without shards
implementation.source: game.js (existing served module), integrated by local/stage.js
implementation.serverNote: OS denied terminating owned 4175 server; reused existing served module/path. Fonts embedded with explicit font/otf data URLs in assets/fonts/bithumb.css so old MIME map is sufficient. Direct OTF MIME added to future server starts.

checks.nativeFontRender: Both provided OTF files registered and rendered through native Canvas; actual Basic/Original glyph difference inspected in dialogue-font-preview.png
checks.fontMime: In-process HTTP handler serves direct OTF font/otf and generated font CSS text/css
checks.shooting: Real Three Raycaster, triangle UV/texture identity, stale font/line completion cancellation, pause, text field shortcut exclusion, hit→burst→disposal→reset lifecycle tested
checks.review: Independent review found two minor issues: temporary impact rotate/scale aiming error and font failure message disappearing; both addressed (XY-only stage shock while targeting, retained error state).

limits.httpAttempt: Sandbox curl could not connect to listening localhost; in-process handler tests passed
limits.preview: Native font/texture inspection, not an actual room or WebGL screenshot
